question.text: A mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> is suspended by a rope of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>, from the ceiling. A force <math><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math> is applied horizontally at the mid-point of the rope such that the top half of the rope makes an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo></math> with the vertical. Then <math><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math> equals: (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> and the rope to be massless)

solution.text:
Let the tension in the string is T.

Applying the condition of equilibrium in the vertical direction,

Tcos45°=100

⇒ T2=100   ...1

In the horizontal direction,

Tsin45°=F

⇒ T2=F

Put the value of T from equation 1,

⇒ F=100 N

So, the horizontal force applied on the rope will be 100 N.
